q: What is BeeZilla?
a: You describe what you want in plain words and BeeZilla does it, asking first only when a big request could easily be misread. It keeps your drafts, decisions and documents together in one place.

q: Is BeeZilla legal or financial advice?
a: No. BeeZilla helps you get the work done, but it is not legal or financial advice. Even the Legal expert says it helps with letters, agreements and notices, not legal advice.

q: How do I start a job?
a: Type what you need into the Talk bar (it says "What would you like to make?") and press Send. Most things BeeZilla just does. For something big that could easily be misread, it first offers one quick choice: a few questions, or just go.

q: What does the Do it button do?
a: Do it tells BeeZilla to stop asking questions and make the thing now, using what it already knows. Pressing "Just go for it" under one of its questions does the same. For work it hands to its agents (a coding project or big research), it still asks one thing first, as a single tap: how much to spend, unless you already said an amount.

sources.symbol: "Just go for it" is the Do it button by another name.
How much should I spend on this, at most? I'll keep my work under that amount.

q: What is the difference between Chat and Work?
a: There's no difference any more: BeeZilla has one mode. For each request it weighs how likely it is to misread you and how costly a mistake would be (more for work other people will see, most for money, health, legal matters, security, people's data or live systems) against the time it takes you to answer. Clear or small things it just does, then shows what it made and lists what it assumed so you can change it. For something big and open it first offers one quick choice: a few questions, or just go. The questions ask why you want it and what it must stay within (time, money, who it's for, what must never happen), never how it should work or anything technical, and each comes with its suggested answer, so one tap accepts it. Anything else you ask meanwhile goes ahead. It remembers your answer for that kind of work, so it asks once. Say "just do it" or press Do it and it goes straight to the work. Work it hands to its agents costs money, so before that starts it asks how much to spend, with three amounts to tap, unless you already named one; that question stays even when you say just go.

q: What can BeeZilla make?
a: Documents (Word), slide decks (PowerPoint) and spreadsheets (Excel). It can also make pictures, music and 3D models when your plan and this site's setup allow it.
limits: Pictures, music and 3D each need their maker to be set up on this site, and pictures and music need a paid plan.

q: Do I need to press a Music or 3D button?
a: No. Just ask, for example "make a song about rain" or "make a 3D model of a chair", and BeeZilla works out which maker to use.

q: How long does a 3D model take?
a: Usually a minute or two. BeeZilla starts it, shows progress in the chat, and the model appears as a download when it is finished.

q: Can I make music on the free plan?
a: No. The free plan has no music. Starter includes 15 minutes a day, up to 3 minutes per track. Pro includes 60 minutes a day, up to 10 minutes per track.

q: How many chats do I get?
a: Free: 100 a day. Starter: 1,000 a day. Pro: 10,000 a day. Open your account menu (your name in the top bar) and the line there shows your plan and how many chats you have left today.

q: Can I make pictures on the free plan?
a: No. The free plan has no picture making. Starter allows 60 pictures a day and Pro allows 400.

q: Where are my files saved?
a: In your Library. It lists what BeeZilla finished for you, newest first: documents, pictures, audio and video. Keep working on it reopens the conversation that made a piece. Every change to a document becomes a new version, and older versions are kept.

q: What file formats can I download?
a: PDF, Word (.docx), Markdown (.md) and CSV, made from the exact version you pick.

q: What does accepting a document mean?
a: Accepting marks one exact version as approved. Only an accepted version can be shared or sent. If the document changes later, you accept the new version again.

q: Can I share a draft that isn't accepted yet?
a: No. Sharing needs an accepted version, so review it and accept it first. That rule is there so a draft never goes out by mistake.

q: What is the Idea Board (formerly the Whiteboard)?
a: It's where BeeZilla's work happens (it used to be called the Whiteboard). Each visit starts with it folded and blank. When you talk or send a message it opens full width and draws what BeeZilla does as it does it: a line to each skill it uses, and what it makes — pictures, music with a waveform, 3D models and documents. Your conversation sits on it as a card you can move and scroll. You can drag anything on the site onto it, edit any card, draw your own process with the tools on the left, and select an area to save it as a recipe. BeeZilla sees the whole board with your next message: your own edits as instructions, and the pictures, music, files and links on it to look at and talk about. To point BeeZilla at something, drag the dot on a card's right edge onto one of its steps: what you connect, it uses there in full, and a connected picture is what it draws from. Make an area around a piece of the board to move, save or share it together; selling an orchestration (for Honey Drops or Honey, or open-sourcing it) is coming soon. You can draw on it too: the Draw tool (D) gives you a pen, shapes and colours, and Make it real turns your drawing into a finished picture beside it. Once you've laid out a few cards, BeeZilla drafts your agent's core identity (how it works here) from them, and a Who it serves card holds who it's working for, which stays private when you share.

q: Is my Idea Board (formerly the Whiteboard) saved to my account?
a: Yes. Each conversation's Idea Board is saved to your account a moment after every change, so it follows you to any computer you sign in on. This browser keeps a copy too, so nothing is lost if the connection drops: it catches up when you're back online. History, the clock by the zoom buttons, keeps earlier versions (the last 30, for up to 90 days), and Go back to this brings one back. Recipes you make from it are saved to your account as well.

q: What can you do?
a: I make things with you by talking: pictures, music, 3D models, short videos, documents, spreadsheets and slides, and I can look things up on the web. Everything I do appears on the Idea Board as I do it, so you can see each step and change any of it, and I can work the board for you when you ask (zoom out, add a note, connect two cards, make an area, start a drawing). Before building something from scratch I check what already exists: your Library, your recipes and simple starting boards. Tell me about one thing you're struggling to do, even if you're not sure I can help with it, and I'll see what I can do about it.

q: What makes BeeZilla unique, and different from other AI tools?
a: Four things. I don't reinvent the wheel: before making something from scratch I look for what has already been done (your Library, your recipes and simple starting boards) and start you from there. You see the work as it happens: the Idea Board draws each step, and you can change any step, connect your own pictures and notes to it, or have me do it by voice. What works becomes yours to keep: cordon off a piece of the board as an orchestration, save it as a recipe, and soon sell it, trade it for Honey Drops or Honey, or open-source it, with what it made shown as examples. And it's one button: Talk to BeeZilla, with Pause and Continue, your own AI key if you want, and privacy modes you control.

q: Can BeeZilla work the Idea Board for me?
a: Yes, just say it. For example: show me the whole board; zoom in on the poster step; add a note saying call the printer; add a step called write the caption; connect the beach photo to the poster step; remove the palette note; rename the step to draw the banner; move the photo next to the poster step; make an area around everything called poster kit; save this as a recipe; sell this orchestration; show the board's history; show the shortcuts; undo; grab my beach photo; start me off with a simple starting board for a logo; start a drawing; turn the drawing into a castle at sunset; who it serves is a bakery in Lisbon; the core identity is friendly and short; open the board; fold the board away. It builds whole orchestrations too, live, card by card: say orchestrate a weekly newsletter, or build me a workflow that answers customer emails, then change it the same way (add a spelling check before my approval, make the writing repeat until it's short enough) and say open it in Orchestrate to check, export or save it. When you're editing a card, press Speak and say what it should say. You watch each step happen, Stop ends it, everything can be undone with Ctrl/⌘+Z, and clearing the whole board waits for your Allow.

q: How do I use the Idea Board's controls?
a: Down the left side are the tools: Select (V), Move the board (H), Note (N), Core identity, who BeeZilla is here (A), Who it serves (P), Skill or step (K), Output, what you want at the end (O), Draw (D) and Upload (U). In the bottom-right corner: zoom out and in, the percentage (back to 100%), Fit everything (Alt/Option+1), History, and the keyboard button (F1) that lists every shortcut. Drag on empty board to select cards; drag a card to move it; double-click a card to edit it (Speak lets you say it instead of typing); double-click a drawing to draw on it; Delete removes; Ctrl/⌘+Z undoes. To connect two cards, drag the dot on a card's right edge onto another card. With cards selected, the bar above them has Create recipe, Make an area, Sell this orchestration and Remove. At the top are the Talk bar, Sell this orchestration and Fold away. Or just tell me what you want and I'll do it.

q: I'm lost on the Idea Board. How do I see everything again?
a: Say “show me the whole board” and I'll zoom out to fit everything, or press Fit everything in the bottom-right corner (Alt/Option+1). Back to 100% is the percentage between the zoom buttons (Ctrl/⌘+0). Select a card and press Alt/Option+2 to zoom to it, or ask me to zoom in on it by name. Hold Space and drag, or use the Move tool (H), to move around.
